entries.who: claims, prior-art, physics and open-problems threads
entries.what: AGENTS.md role A2 makes an orx literature run a release requirement: before a claim is formalised or tested it must carry a logged run saying what the modern literature already says about it. The stated reason is that the biggest credibility risk here is restating a historical claim as though nobody had studied it since.
entries.evidence: 86 `orx discover` calls against OpenAlex, PubMed and the alphaXiv corpus: 6 for the headline claim tests, 59 for organism-design prior art, 9 for the physics thread, 12 for the open-problems catalogue. Also a full orx experiment record for the Collier 1996 replay (run_id, experiment_id, SHA-256 of model and log, all_checks_passed true, 2026-10-31T19:04:19Z).
entries.limit: No orx experiment or compute run beyond that replay — `discover` only — and no alphaXiv GPU credits. Grounding covers the six headline tests, the design idea, physics and open problems, NOT all 174 tested claims.
entries.note: The headline finding is a negative one and it changed the pitch: 5 of the 6 headline claims were ALREADY ANSWERED by prior work, so those tests are presented as reproductions rather than discoveries. Prior-art search also killed the claim of a 'first formal verification of biology' — Phenoscape is the closest prior work and is now cited.

entries.tool: Nebius Scientific AI Platform (Cellpose, CPSAM v2)
entries.where: cell segmentation for three Thompson claims
entries.what: Called through the Nebius MCP server from plugins/nebius/, with content-derived idempotency keys so a crashed or re-run script re-attaches to the same operation instead of starting new work.
entries.evidence: 19 Nebius operations: 8 openly licensed tissue micrographs plus 11 synthetic tilings for a segmenter-bias null. Each record carries the Nebius operation_id, the model SHA-256, the Cellpose version and the SHA-256 of the exact input image, so every mask traces to its run. Three signed evidence nanopubs carry the operation IDs.
entries.limit: Two of the three verdicts are weaker than they look: ch07-08 holds but is a property of ANY space-filling partition (the random Voronoi control shows it too), and ch07-10 is forced by Euler's formula.
entries.note: The best result here is a self-inflicted downgrade. An outside agent asked for a segmenter-bias null; it was run on Nebius with the same checkpoint and showed Cellpose rounds corners toward Y-junctions — pulling even a BRICK WALL toward 120 degrees. The ch07-04 confidence was cut from 0.60 to 0.35 as a result.

entries.what: A self-hosted dataset-resolvability assessor on an L40S instance, JSON-schema constrained, about one claim per second at concurrency 24.
entries.evidence: All 566 claims of the Aristotle biology project assessed, with the assessor recorded as open weights served on our own GPU.
entries.limit: Qwen's thinking mode was off in all runs and was never compared against.
entries.note: The point is the pipeline rule assessor != builder, with at least two assessor providers. An open-weights model on our own GPU is a provider no frontier-API builder shares.

entries.what: Ranks the synonymous codon options and silent blocking-mutation sets for an edit plan by genomic-language-model likelihood, and scores the edited locus against the reference.
entries.evidence: Live against health.api.nvidia.com. On kcnk5b p.W169L the edit lowers locus likelihood by 0.184 per base, and Evo2's codon preference DISAGREES with our hand rule — it puts CTT first, which our rule ranked fifth of six.
entries.limit: It RANKS, it never GATES. A likelihood says the sequence looks like the genomes the model was trained on: not a phenotype prediction, not safety, not specificity, not calibrated, and no threshold is asserted.
entries.note: There is no scoring route on the NIM, so the likelihood is computed by teacher forcing through /generate — one call per base, with the byte-vocabulary mapping verified against the live endpoint rather than assumed.

entries.what: Two dragonfly hindwings — one with venation segmented from a photograph, one with cross veins regenerated by the Hoffmann 2018 rule — plus flying zebrafish, and the 1:1 and 120 mm kits.
entries.evidence: Both wings printed at 140 mm, 0.6 mm membrane, 1.5 mm at the main veins, photographed onto issue #58.
entries.limit: The scan comparison has only passed on a SIMULATED scan, so there is no measured agreement between print and design or between the two prints. The flying zebrafish prints are reported by the project lead and not yet photographed into the repo. A measured 3.8% size mismatch is recorded rather than corrected.
